rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prostration is the highest degree of worship, so it must be reserved for God alone.
rows.anchor: فإن السجود أقصى مراتب العبادة فلا بد من تخصيصه به عز وجل

rows.speaker: علي وابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ali and Ibn Masud used to prostrate at the end of this verse, at taʿbudūn.
rows.anchor: وكان علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه وابن مسعود يسجدان عند ( تعبدون )

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: The view that the prostration point is taʿbudūn is attributed to al-Shafiʿi.
rows.anchor: ونسب القول بأنه موضع السجدة للشافعي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وابن عمر وأبو وائل وبكر بن عبد الله وابن وهب ومسروق والسلمي والنخعي وأبو صالح وابن وثاب والحسن وابن سيرين وأبو حنيفة
rows.claim: These authorities are reported to prostrate at lā yasʾamūn in the following verse.
rows.anchor: وسجد عند ( لا يسأمون ) ابن عباس وابن عمر وأبو وائل وبكر بن عبد الله

rows.speaker: أصحاب الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Kashf calls lā yasʾamūn the sounder of the two Shafiʿi positions, matching Abu Hanifa's view.
rows.anchor: وفي الكشف أصح الوجحهين عند أصحابنا يعني الشافعية أن موضع السجدة ( لا يسأمون ) كما هو مذهب الإمام أبي حنيفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The later point completes the meaning and fits the command to prostrate, since arrogance toward prostration is blameworthy.
rows.anchor: ووجهه أنها تمام المعنى على أسلوب اسجد فإن الإستكبار عنه مذموم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some explain the later prostration point as precaution: delay is allowed if the earlier point is intended, but advancing it is not allowed if the later point is intended.
rows.anchor: وعلله بعضهم بالإحتياط لأنها إن كانت عند ( تعبدون ) جاز التأخير لقصر الفصل وإن كانت عند ( يسأمون ) لم يجز تعجيلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If God expanded provision, people would grow arrogant and exceed the limits fitting for servants, or wrong one another; wealth readily breeds insolence and pride.
rows.anchor: أي لتكبروا فيها بطرا وتجاوز الحد الذي يليق بالعبيد أو لظلم بعضهم بعضا فإن الغني مبطرة مأشرة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A hadith says the Prophet most feared worldly abundance and its increase for his community.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث أخوف ما أخاف على أمتي زهرة الدنيا وكثرتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An Arab poetic line about the wasmi rain growing plants precedes the gloss that baghy is seeking more than one's due, in amount or quality.
rows.anchor: ولبعض العرب : وقد جعل الوسمي ينبت بيننا وبين بني روماننبعاوشوحطا وأصلا لبغي طلب أكثر مما يجب

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read yunazzilu without doubling, from anzala; the majority read it doubled.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو بالتخفيف من الأنزال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bi-qadar means by a measured determination of what God's wisdom requires.
rows.anchor: بقدر ( بتقدير ( ما يشاء ( وهوما اقتضته حكمته جل شأنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows servants' hidden and manifest circumstances and apportions each person's provision at each time as befits them, withholding or giving, contracting or expanding, in accord with divine wisdom.
rows.anchor: محيط بخفيات أمورهم وجلاياها فيقدر لكل واحدمنهم فيكل وقت من أوقاتهم ما يليق بشأنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Universal enrichment would bring transgression, while universal poverty would bring ruin; either extreme disrupts the order of the world.
rows.anchor: ولو أغناهم جميعا لبغوا ولو أفقرهم لهلكوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An objection says poverty too can cause transgression, so the verse's conditional relation is not self-evident.
rows.anchor: واستشكلت الآية بأن الغنى كما يكون سبب البغي فذلك الفقر قد يكون فلا يظهر الشرطية

rows.speaker: جار الله
rows.claim: Jar Allah answers that transgression is less likely under poverty and more likely under abundance; if abundance were universal, transgression would predominate and reverse the present order.
rows.anchor: وأجاب جار الله بأنه لا شبهة أن البغي مع الفقر أقل ومع البسط أكثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author explains that the current mixed distribution checks wrongdoing: fear of the poor restrains the rich, while the poor's greater dependence on the rich encourages cooperation and curbs their own excess.
rows.anchor: وأما الذي عليه سنة الله عز وجل فهو الذي جمع الأمرين مشتملا على خوف للغني من الفقراء يزعه عن الظلم

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشف
rows.claim: The author endorses the Kashf explanation as a sound answer without forced reasoning and uses it to reject al-Tibi's criticism that the objection is strong and its answer strained.
rows.anchor: كذا قرره صاحب الكشف ثم قال : وهذا جواب حسن لا تكلف فيه وهو إشارة إلى رد العلامة الطيبي

rows.speaker: الطيبي
rows.claim: Al-Tibi takes ʿibādihi here as servants specially honored by God and made His friends; the closing words indicate God's knowledge of their circumstances and what benefits or harms them.
rows.anchor: وذهب هو إلى أن المراد ( بعباده ) من خصهم الله تعالى بالكرامة وجعلهم من أوليائه

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report says that when God loves a servant, He protects him from worldly life as one protects a sick person from water.
rows.anchor: إذاأحب الله تعالى عبداحماه الدنياكمايظل أحدكم يحمي سقيمه الماء

rows.speaker: خباب بن الأرت
rows.claim: Khabbab said they saw the wealth of Qurayza, Nadir, and Qaynuqa and wished for it; the verse was then revealed.
rows.anchor: ويشد من عضده قولخباب بن الأرت نظرناإلى أموال بني قريظة والنضير وبنيقينقاعفتمنيناها فنزلت

rows.speaker: عمرو بن حريث
rows.claim: Amr ibn Hurayth says people of the Suffa asked the Messenger to enrich them and expand their provision, after which the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: وقول عمرو ابنحريث طلب قوم من أهل الصفة من الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يغنيهمالله تعالى ويبسط لهم الأموال والأرزاقفنزلت

rows.speaker: محيي السنة
rows.claim: The interpretation that the servants singled out are God's honored friends is also attributed to Muhyi al-Sunna.
rows.anchor: وعليه تفسير محيي السنة انتهى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author finds the general explanation more fitting, since God's elect are unlikely to be intoxicated by wealth; alternatively, the warning can concern some believing servants.
rows.anchor: فلعل الأولى ما تقدمأو يقال : إن هذا في بعض العباد المؤمنين فتأمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghayth is rain that brings relief from drought and is beneficial; not every kind of rain is called ghayth.
rows.anchor: أيالمطرالذي يغيثهممن الجدب ولذلك خصبالنافع منه فلا يقال غيث لكل مطر

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read yunazzilu with a light consonant, without doubling.
rows.anchor: وقرأالجمهور ( ينزل ) مخففا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning that the rain comes after people despair of it recalls God's favor, though the rain also descends at other times.
rows.anchor: وتقييد تنزيلهبذلك معتحققه بدونهأيض التذكير النعمة

rows.speaker: الأعمش وابن وثاب
rows.claim: Al-Aʿmash and Ibn Waththab read qanitu with kasra on the nūn.
rows.anchor: وقرأالأعمش وابن وثاب ( قنطوا ) بكسرالنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God spreads the rain's benefits and effects through plains, mountains, plants, and animals; alternatively, this refers broadly to His encompassing mercy, of which those are a primary instance.
rows.anchor: أي منافع الغيثوآثاره في كلشيء من السهل والجبل والنبات والحيوان أو رحمته الواسعة المنتظمة لما ذكر انتظاماأوليا

rows.speaker: المهدوي
rows.claim: Al-Mahdawi says the mercy is the sun appearing after prolonged rain has wearied people; the author rejects this as unsound.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الرحمة هناظهورالشمس لأنهإذادام المطرسئمفتجيء الشمس بعده عظيمة الموقع ذكره المهدوي وليس بشيء

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi identifies the mercy as the rain itself, which the author calls very far-fetched because it repeats the same blessing in two expressions.
rows.anchor: ومنالبعيد جداما قاله السدي من أن الرحمة هنا الغيث نفسه عدد النعمة نفسها بلفظين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in His mercy refers to God; under the first interpretation of mercy's spread, it may instead refer to the rain.
rows.anchor: فضمير ) رحمته للهعز وجل وجوز على الأول كونه للغيث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Wali is the one who benevolently tends His servants and spreads mercy; al-Hamid is the one alone deserving praise for this.
rows.anchor: وهو الولي ( الذييتولى عباده بالأحسان ونشرالرحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the ordinary sense of istikhfāf, Pharaoh sought their eagerness and quickness to comply; khiffa here means speed in answering and following, a familiar metaphor.
rows.anchor: فطلب منهم الخفة في مطاوعته على أن السين للطلب على حقيقتها ومعنى الخفة السرعة لأجابته ومتابعته

rows.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Aʿrabi explains that Pharaoh found their intellects light, meaning deficient; the form denotes finding, as in ahmadtu, and attributing that to the people is figurative.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن الأعرابي استخف أحلامهم أيوجدهم خفيفة أحلامهم أي قليلة عقولهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They obeyed Pharaoh in what he commanded them.
rows.anchor: فاطاعوه ( فيما أمرهم به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their own transgression explains why they hurried to obey the transgressing, misguided Pharaoh.
rows.anchor: فلذلك سارعوا إلى طاعة ذلك الفاسق الغوي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Take him is an implied quotation addressed to the wardens: they are told, Take him.
rows.anchor: على إرادة القول والمقول له الزبانية أي ويقال لهم خذوه

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib defines ʿatl as seizing something and dragging it forcefully; specifying a garment is unnecessary, since violent dragging while holding it is the core sense.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب : العتل الأخذ بمجامع الشيء وجره بقهر

rows.speaker: الأعمش ومجاهد
rows.claim: Al-Aʿmash and Mujahid gloss it as breaking him as one breaks firewood; the author notes that this requires implication or attachment of the prepositional phrase to take him, while dragging is the familiar sense.
rows.anchor: وقال اتل أعمش ومجاهد : معنى ( اعتلوه ) اقصفوه كما يقصف الحطب

rows.speaker: زيد بن علي والحجازيان وابن عامر ويعقوب
rows.claim: These readers pronounce the tāʾ with ḍamma; the reading with fatḥ is the majority form, and both are dialectal patterns.
rows.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي والحجازيان وابن عامر ويعقوب ( فاعتلوه ) ) بضم التاء

rows.speaker: الحسن وقتادة والأعرج
rows.claim: The ḍamma reading is also transmitted from al-Hasan, Qatada, and al-Aʿraj.
rows.anchor: وروي ذلك عن الحسن وقتادة والأعرج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sawāʾ al-Jahim means its middle, called sawāʾ because it is equidistant from all sides.
rows.anchor: أيوسطه وسمي سواء لاستواء بعد جميع أطرافه بالنسبة إليه

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima reports that Abu Jahl boasted to the Prophet that neither he nor his companion could harm him, since he protected the people of the valley and was noble; after Badr, God humiliated him with this taunt.
rows.anchor: عن عكرمة أن أبا جهل قال للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : ما تستطيع لي أنت ولاصاحبك من شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another report says Abu Jahl asked Quraysh to guess his name, rejected Umar, al-Jallas, and Abu al-Hakam, then called himself al-Aziz al-Karim; the verses about the tree of Zaqqūm then came down.
rows.anchor: وروي أن اللعين قال يوما : يا معشر قريش أخبروني ما اسمي فذكرت له ثلاثة أسماء عمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse is not restricted to Abu Jahl: every sinner who makes a similar claim will be addressed this way at the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: وهذا ونحوه لا يد لأيضاع لى تخصيص حكم الآية به فكل أثيم يدعى دعواه كذلك يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is: taste this, though you were mighty among your people and honored by them; that status did not benefit you. Tasting is a metaphor for experiencing.
rows.anchor: وقيل : المعنى ذق إنك العزيز في قومك الكريم عليهم فما أغنى ذلك عنك ولم يفدك شيئا

rows.speaker: الحسن بن علي بن أبي طالب والكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Hasan ibn Ali and al-Kisaʾi read anna with fatḥa on the hamza, understood as because you are.
rows.anchor: وقرأالحسنبن علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله تعالى عنهما على المنبرو الكسائي ( أنك ) بفتح الهمزة على معنى لأنك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The listeners are hypocrites; the singular in يستمع follows the word's grammatical form, while the later plural follows its meaning.
rows.anchor: هم المنافقون وإفراد الضمير باعتبار اللفظ كما أن جمعه بعد باعتبار المعنى

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj says they attended the Messenger's gathering and heard him but paid no heed or proper attention out of disdain.
rows.anchor: قال ابن جريج : كانوا يحضرون مجلس رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم فيسمعون كلامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those given knowledge are the learned Companions; alternatively, they are the Companions who attended to the Prophet's speech with due care.
rows.anchor: أي لأولي العلم من الصحابة رضي الله تعالى عنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question usually feigns inquiry to mock the Prophet; it may instead be a genuine question from inattention, which is why they are still condemned, but the mocking reading is preferred.
rows.anchor: ومقصودهم من ذك الأستهزاء وإن كان بصورة الأستعلام وجوز أن يكون مرادهم حقيقة الأستعلام

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says he himself is among those given knowledge and named among those asked about the Prophet's words.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أنا منهم وقد سميت فيمن سئل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anifan is a non-regular active participle, or one formed after removing the derived prefix, since only istaʾnafa and atʾanafa are attested verbs.
rows.anchor: لم يسمع له فعل ثلاثي بل استأنف وأتنف

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj derives anifan from istaʾnaft al-shayʾ, to begin something: its original image is taking its nose or beginning, then nose came to mean a thing's front or foremost part.
rows.anchor: وذكر الزجاج أنه من استأنفت الشيء إذا ابتدأته وكان أصل معنى هذا أخذت أنفه

rows.speaker: غير واحد
rows.claim: Several authorities explain anifan as the time just before the present, by metaphor from the nose's forward position; another view makes it the present moment.
rows.anchor: وذكر غير واحد أن آنفا من ذلك قالوا : إنه للساعة التي قبل ساعتك التي أنت فيها

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari treats anifan as an adverb of time, which is compatible with its participial form because such forms can be lexicalized as adverbs.
rows.anchor: وهو على ما ذهب إليه الزمخشري نصب على الظرفية ولا ينافي كونه اسم فاعل

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan says it is not an adverb, since grammarians do not classify it as one; it is a circumstantial accusative of the speaker, meaning what he had just begun saying before they left.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو حيان : الصحيح أنه ليس بظرف ولا نعلم أحدا من النحاة عده

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir reads anifan on the faʿl pattern.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير ( آنفا على وزن فعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They turned toward everything devoid of good, which explains their conduct.
rows.anchor: فتوجهوا نحو كل ما لا خير فيه فلذلك كان منهم ما كان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those guided to the way of truth are increased by God in guidance through enabling and inspiration.
rows.anchor: إلى طريق الحق ( زادهم ( أي الله عز وجل ( هدى ( بالتوفيق والإلهام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relative clause can be nominative as subject or accusative after an omitted verb explained by the following verb; the apparent reading is nominative. Hudan is either the second object of zāda or a specification, with the former more apparent, and its indefinite form magnifies it.
rows.anchor: والموصول يحتمل الرفع على الأبتداء والنصب بفعل محذوف يفسره المذكور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's giving them taqwa can mean creating it in them, as Ashʿaris say of human acts, or creating in them an effective capacity by His permission, as al-Kurani attributes to al-Ashʿari and other investigators; making them God-fearing can fit either account.
rows.anchor: بأن خلقها فيهم بناء على ما يقوله الأشاعرة في أفعال العباد

rows.speaker: البيضاوي
rows.claim: Al-Baydawi offers three readings: God showed them what to avoid, helped them practice taqwa, or gave them its reward; the wording is figurative in the first two, or literal reward because taqwa causes it, or has an omitted possessive. None conflicts with orthodox doctrine.
rows.anchor: وقال البيضاوي : أي بين لهم ما يتقون أو أعانهم على تقواهم

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari mentions helping them in taqwa and giving them its reward from al-Baydawi's alternatives.
rows.anchor: وذكر الزمخشري الثاني والثالث من ذلك

rows.speaker: الطيبي
rows.claim: Al-Tibi favors the help interpretation: it pairs following desires with receiving taqwa, while sealed hearts pair with increased guidance; perfected taqwa means the knower turns wholly to God, as in the command to fear Him as He deserves.
rows.anchor: واختار الطيبي الأول من هذين الأثنين وقال : هو أوفق لتأليف النظم الكريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says this contrastive arrangement also works with his explanations and with taqwa as guidance about what to avoid; interpreting it as the reward of taqwa is reported from Saʿid ibn Jubayr and al-Jubbaʾi and is more informative without inflating taqwa to its highest degree.
rows.anchor: وتفسير ذلك بإعطاء جزاء التقوى مروي عن سعيد بن جبير وذهب إليه الجبائي والكلام عليه أفيد

rows.speaker: الطيبي
rows.claim: Al-Tibi pairs those guided against those who followed desires, and increased guidance against hearts sealed; the author says this alignment can also explain the passage without making contrast decisive.
rows.anchor: إن قوله تعالى ( اهتدوا ) في مقابلة ( اتبعوا أهواءهم ) وقوله سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view makes the Prophet, understood from the preceding address, the subject of increased guidance and the giving of taqwa, with a figurative attribution; the author calls it contrary to the apparent sense and says the subject should align with God's sealing of hearts.
rows.anchor: وقيل : فاعل ( زادهم ) ضمير قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم المفهوم من قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A very remote suggestion makes the subject the hypocrites' remark, since it might amaze believers and increase their conviction; the author says it is scarcely worth considering.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن يكون ضميرا عائدا على قول المنافقين فإن ذلك مما يعجب منه المؤمن

rows.speaker: الطيبي
rows.claim: Al-Tibi reads renouncing desire as turning toward the Master and leaving worldly cravings; following desire is spiritual illness, while abiding by taqwa is divine medicine.
rows.anchor: العزوب عن شهوات الحياة الدنيا ثم في إسناد إيتاء التقوى إليه تعالى وإسناد متابعة الهوى إليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All people descend from Adam and Eve and are equal in that origin, so lineage is no basis for boasting.
rows.anchor: من آدم وحواء عليهما السلام فالكل سواء في ذلك فلا وجه للتفاخر بالنسب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poetic saying expresses the same equality: people are peers, with Adam as father and Eve as mother.
rows.anchor: الناس في عالم التمثيل أكفاء أبوهم آدم والأم حواء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that each person was created from one father and one mother; the author finds it weak because it does not explain the rebuke of lineage pride.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن يكون المراد هنا إنا خلقنا كل واحد منكم من أب وأم ويبعده عدم ظهور ترتب ذم التفاخر بالنسب عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further view takes the phrase as establishing brotherhood that bars backbiting; its connection to what follows is less strong than the shared-origin explanation, though the brotherhood point is clear.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هو تقرير للأخوة المانعة عن الأغتياب وعدم ظهور الترتب عليه على حاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the main genealogical usage, a shaʿb is a great group tracing to one ancestor and encompassing tribes; a tribe encompasses ʿamāʾir, then clans, subclans, and families. The author illustrates the ranks with Khuzaima, Kinana, Quraysh, Qusayy, Hashim, and al-Abbas.
rows.anchor: وهم الجمع العظيم المنتسبون إلى أصل واحد وهو يجمع القبائل والقبيلة تجمع العمائر والعمارة بفتح العين وقد تكسر تجمع البطون

rows.speaker: بعض الأدباء
rows.claim: A literary poet lists the descent order as tribe, shaʿb, ʿimāra, clan, and subclan, then says a man is sheltered by his family and an arrow needs its feathers to fly straight.
rows.anchor: قبيلة فوقها شعب وبعدها عمارة ثم بطن تلوه فخذ وليس يؤوي الفتى إلا فصيلته

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another poem adds ʿashira after family and recites the sequence from shaʿb through tribe, ʿimāra, clan, subclan, family, and ʿashira.
rows.anchor: أقصد الشعب فهو أكثر حي عددا في الحساب ثم القبيلة ثم يتلوهما العمارة ثم البطن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The name shuʿub is explained by the tribes branching out from them.
rows.anchor: وسميت الشعوب لأنالقبائل تشبعت منها

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة عن ابن الكلبي عن أبيه
rows.claim: A lineage ranking relayed by Abu Ubayda from Ibn al-Kalbi and his father places the family before ʿimāra and ʿimāra before subclan, unlike the preceding arrangement.
rows.anchor: وحكى أبو عبيدة عن ابن الكلبي عن أبيه تقديم الشعب ثم القبيلة ثم الفصيلة ثم العمارة

rows.speaker: مسروق
rows.claim: Masruq relates that a man from the shuʿub became Muslim and was charged jizya; al-Alusi cites this to support the non-Arab interpretation of shuʿub.
rows.anchor: وأيد كون الشعوب في العجم ما في حديث مسروق أن رجلا من الشعوب أسلم فكانت تؤخذ منه الجزية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One possibility makes shuʿub the plural of shuʿubi: someone, such as a Jew or Magian, who belittles Arabs and denies their superiority; Abu Ubayda wrote a book attacking Arabs, and Ibn Garsiya argued for non-Arabs, prompting Andalusian refutations.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون جمع الشعوبي وهو الذي يصغر شأن العرب ولا يرى لهم فضلا على غيرهم كيهود ومجوس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view identifies shuʿub with the Arabs of Yemen descended from Qahtan and the tribes with Rabiʿa, Mudar, and the rest of Adnan.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الشعوب عرب اليمن من قحطان والقبائل ربيعة ومضر وسائر عدنان

rows.speaker: قتادة ومجاهد والضحاك
rows.claim: Qatada, Mujahid, and al-Dahhak say shaʿb denotes the more remote ancestry and qabila the nearer.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة ومجاهد والضحاك : الشعب النسب إلا بعد والقبيلة الأقرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes shuʿub as non-Arab clients and qabilas as Arabs.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الشعوب الموالي والقبائل العرب

rows.speaker: أبو روق
rows.claim: Abu Rawq says shuʿub are those tracing ancestry to towns and villages, while Arab tribes trace themselves to fathers.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو روق : الشعوب الذين ينتسبون إلى المدائن والقرى والقبائل العرب الذين ينتسبون إلى آبائهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purpose of the social groupings is mutual recognition, kinship ties, identifying genealogies, and inheritance, not boasting about forebears and tribes; this restriction is inferred from what is specified and what is left unsaid.
rows.anchor: علة للجعل أي جعلناكم كذلك ليعرف بعضكم بعضا فتصلوا الأرحام وتبينوا الأنساب والتوارث لا لتفاخروا بالآباء والقبائل

rows.speaker: الأعمش
rows.claim: Al-Aʿmash reads litataʿarafu with two tāʾs, preserving the original form.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش ( لتتعارفوا ) بتاءين على الأصل

rows.speaker: مجاهد وابن كثير في رواية وابن محيصن
rows.claim: Mujahid, Ibn Kathir in one transmission, and Ibn Muhaysin assimilate the two tāʾs.
rows.anchor: ومجاهد وابن كثير في رواية وابن محيصن بإدغام التاء في التاء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وأبان عن عاصم
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Aban from Asim read li-taʿrafu with kasra on the rāʾ.
rows.anchor: وابن عباس وأبان عن عاصم ( لتعرفوا ) بكسر الراء

rows.speaker: ابن جني
rows.claim: Ibn Jinni says the object of taʿrafu is omitted, as in the poetic line meaning that a person learns only in order to know what he has learned; the author estimates the object as the kinship among you.
rows.anchor: قال ابن جني : والمفعول محذوف أي لتعرفوا ما أنتم محتاجون إليه كقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This clause justifies rejecting lineage pride: the most honored and highest in rank before God in this life and the next is the most God-fearing, so anyone seeking high rank should pursue taqwa.
rows.anchor: تعليل للنهي عن التفاخر بالأنساب المستفاد من الكلام بطريق الأستئناف الحقيقي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reads anna with fatḥa, supplying a causal lām: they should not boast by ancestry because the most honored before God is the most pious.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس ( أن ) بفتح الهمزة على حذف لام التعليل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Bahr reports Ibn Abbas reading both li-taʿrafu and anna-akramakum; it suggests the latter clause is the object of an imperative li-taʿrafu, which the author finds semantically better than a causal lām. A causal reading could work if the omitted object is al-haqq.
rows.anchor: وفي البحر أن ابن عباس قرأ ( لتعرفوا وأنأكرمكم ) بفتح الهمزة فاحتمل أن يكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is knowing of people and their deeds, and fully aware of their inward states.
rows.anchor: إن الله عليم ( بكم وبأعمالكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A conquest-of-Mecca occasion report says al-Harith ibn Hisham and Attab ibn Asid objected angrily when Bilal called the prayer from atop the Kaaba, calling him a black slave; this verse then came down.
rows.anchor: لما كان يوم فتح مكة أذن بلال على الكعبة فغضب الحرث بن هشام وعتاب بن أسيد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas gives as occasion that Thabit ibn Qays insulted a man who did not make room before the Prophet by calling him the son of a certain woman; the Prophet rebuked him and said superiority is only through religion and taqwa.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس سبب نزولها قول ثابت بن قيس لرجل لم يفسح له عند النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم يا ابن فلانة

rows.speaker: الزهري
rows.claim: Al-Zuhri reports that the Prophet instructed Banu Bayada to marry Abu Hind, his cupper, to a woman among them; they objected to marrying their daughters to clients, and the verse was revealed, specifically for Abu Hind according to al-Zuhri.
rows.anchor: عن الزهري قال : أمر رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم بني بياضة

rows.speaker: عروة عن عائشة
rows.claim: A report through Urwa from Aisha says the Prophet commanded that Abu Hind be married into a family and that a woman be married to him, after which this verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: عن عروة عن عائشة أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام قال : أنكحوا أبا هند

rows.speaker: يزيد بن شجرة
rows.claim: Yazid ibn Shajara relates that the Prophet bought a black boy who required that he not be kept from the five prayers behind him; after the boy fell ill and died, the Prophet washed and buried him, deeply affecting the Emigrants and Helpers, and the verse was revealed. The author doubts the report's soundness.
rows.anchor: وعن يزيد بن شجرة مر رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse rules out pride in ancestry, as prophetic reports also make clear.
rows.anchor: وقد دلت على أنه لا ينبغي التفاخر بالأنساب وبذلك نطقت الأخبار

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Umar reports that at the conquest the Prophet praised God for removing pre-Islamic disgrace and arrogance, said people are either pious and noble before God or sinful and low, and affirmed that all are children of Adam created from dust before reciting this verse.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عمر أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم طاف يوم الفتح على راحلته

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: Jabir says the Prophet declared in the Farewell Sermon that the Lord is one, no Arab or non-Arab and no black or red person has precedence over another except by taqwa, then asked witnesses to convey the message.
rows.anchor: وأخرج البيهقي وابن مردويه عن جابر بن عبد الله قال : خطبنا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في وسط أيام التشريق

rows.speaker: أبو أمامة
rows.claim: Abu Umama reports the Prophet saying God removed the arrogance of pre-Islamic lineage, all people descend from Adam and Eve, and the most honored is the most pious; he also urged marriage to a suitor whose religion and trustworthiness are approved.
rows.anchor: وأخرج البيهقي عن أبي أمامة قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إن الله أذهب نخوة الجاهلية وتكبرها بآبائها

rows.speaker: أحمد وجماعة
rows.claim: Ahmad and others transmit a similar report, but omit the instruction about marrying a suitor whose religion and trustworthiness are approved.
rows.anchor: وأخرج أحمد وجماعة نحوه لكن ليس فيه فمن أتاكم الخ
